data.title: Test Coverage
data.tagline: Test coverage measures how much of requirements, code structure, or risk paths have been reached by tests.
data.learningOutcome: You can turn one coverage number into a question about which high-risk paths are tested and which are not.
data.description: Branch coverage can show whether the coupon-plus-payment-failure combination was reached; a requirements matrix can show a missing payment case. Coverage finds untouched paths. It does not mean no defect or meaningful assertions, even at 100%.

learning.assumes: You know one feature can have success, failure, and boundary paths.
learning.outcome: You can turn one coverage number into a question about which high-risk paths are tested and which are not.

distinctions.label: Unit test
distinctions.explanation: Test Coverage measures the scope that tests reach. A Unit Test is an actual kind of test, and high coverage cannot prove that its assertions are correct.

explanation.title: Coverage shows reach, not reliable outcome
explanation.text: A code line or branch executed only means a test passed through it. Without checking the right result or modeling a real risk, a high number cannot prove payment behavior is right.

explanation.title: Fill untested high-risk paths first
explanation.text: Inspect real risks such as coupon combinations, payment failure, and insufficient permission rather than pursuing one global percentage. A map of tested and untested requirements guides action better than a number alone.

data.boundary: Test coverage is neither test pass rate nor proof of no bugs. It only states reach; quality also depends on assertions, test data, environment, and whether important user risks are covered.

lessonPractice.title: A report says 100% code coverage, but the page still says “order succeeded” when payment fails. What is the best conclusion?

options.label: Check whether the failure branch asserts page state, then add an observable result for failed payment
options.feedback: Correct. A test may execute the failure branch without checking that the page gives the right feedback.

options.label: Confirm the failure branch runs, then run it more often to reinforce the 100% coverage number
options.feedback: Repeated execution still only proves the code was reached. Without a useful assertion, the wrong success message remains invisible.

options.label: Keep the current coverage and record this error as a separate manual check without changing automated tests
options.feedback: A manual record preserves the symptom, but this stable failure path still lacks an automated check of the user result.

data.agentPrompt: Report payment-flow coverage, not only a percentage: list whether success, payment failure, coupon combination, and insufficient permission are tested. Prioritize untested high-risk branches and verify each user-visible result.
